textual_delivery_p2_review.dialogue_context_basis: Harry's flat denial of any gruesome courtroom cases contrasts with the reporter's enthusiastic hunting for gore.
Harry jokes that the bloodthirsty reporter must be bored with television rather than legitimately interested in court.
Craven celebrates finding inexhaustible human misery, a macabre professional self-description.
Craven turns the suffering of others into the setup for another morbid observation.
Harry's clipped reply gently punctures Craven's morbid enthusiasm.
Harry answers a request for his age by claiming to be more than nine centuries old.
Harry extends his ancient-soul absurdity by declaring his first centuries a blur.
